examples.en: The kids are playing soccer in the yard.
My brother plays the guitar.

related.en: to play a game or sport, with acc. — игра́ть в футбо́л, в ша́хматы
to play an instrument, with prep. — игра́ть на гита́ре, на пиани́но

note: The preposition decides: в + acc. for games and sports, на + prep. for instruments.

examples.en: My brother got married last year.
She married a doctor.
They got married in May.

related.en: to get married (of a man) — жени́ться на + prep.
to get married (of a woman) — вы́йти за́муж за + acc.
to get married (of both) — они́ пожени́лись

note: There is no single verb for both sexes: a man жени́ться, a woman вы́йти за́муж. The state is said differently: он жена́т, она́ за́мужем.

examples.en: I want to eat.
Please, help yourself!

related.en: to eat — the general, neutral verb: я ем
to eat, politely — when offering food to a guest or a child

note: About yourself say я ем: я ку́шаю sounds overly refined. Ку́шать is for inviting someone else: ку́шай, ку́шайте.

examples.en: Show me a different jacket, please.
He lives on the second floor.

related.en: other, different, another — друго́й вопро́с
second in order, next in a series — второ́й день

note: If you count in order, say второ́й: второ́й день is the second day in a row. If you mean «some other», say друго́й: друго́й день is a different day.

examples.en: That was the last bus.
He lives in the last house at the end of the street.

related.en: last in time or in a sequence — после́дний раз
outermost, at the very edge — кра́йний дом

note: Кра́йний marks the outermost place in space. In a queue people colloquially ask кто кра́йний? - who is last? For the end of a period of time use после́дний раз.

examples.en: I remember that day well.
We often think back on our student years.
He reminds me of my brother.

related.en: to remember, to keep in mind — a state: я по́мню его́
to recall, to bring back to mind — вспомина́ть де́тство
to remind someone of something; to resemble

examples.en: He is finishing school this year.
We finish work at six.

related.en: to finish, colloquial — pf. ко́нчить
to finish, neutral — pf. зако́нчить

note: Ко́нчить with no object («я ко́нчил») can be understood as vulgar, so when in doubt say зако́нчить.

examples.en: We live in an old house.
An elderly man was sitting on the bus.

related.en: old — of things and of people
elderly, getting on in years — a polite word for a person

note: Ста́рый said of a person can sound rude, so for a polite word use пожило́й. Ста́рый друг is «an old friend», not «an old man».

examples.en: He is a very kind person.
All people are different.
There were five people in the room.

related.en: person, human being — one individual
people — the plural of челове́к

note: The plural of челове́к is лю́ди, not «человеки». With five and more the counted form is челове́к: пять челове́к, but два челове́ка.

examples.en: We have one child.
Our children go to school.

related.en: child, one
children — the plural of ребёнок

note: The plural of ребёнок is де́ти. Two is два ребёнка, but five is пять дете́й. Ребя́та also means «guys, folks»: ребя́та, пойдёмте!

examples.en: He is the man who helped me.
What's the date today?

related.en: who, which in a relative clause; which in order
what kind of, which of several — in a question about type or choice

note: Кото́рый is «who, which» in a relative clause (челове́к, кото́рый звони́л); како́й asks «what kind of» or «which» (како́й фильм?). «What time is it?» is Кото́рый час?.

examples.ru: [Е́сли] у тебя будет время, позвони мне.
examples.en: If you have time, call me.
I don't know whether he will come.

related.en: if — a condition
whether — a question, placed after the word it refers to

note: «I don't know whether he will come» is не зна́ю, придёт ли он, not «если он придёт». Если only means «if».

examples.en: He said that he would come later.
I want you to come.

related.en: that — after verbs of saying and thinking: он сказа́л, что...
so that, to — a wish, purpose or order: хочу́, что́бы...

note: Russian has two words for «that»: что for a fact and что́бы for a wish or purpose. After что́бы the verb takes the past-tense form: хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл.

examples.en: I didn't come because I was sick.
He was sick, so he didn't come.

related.en: because — gives the cause
so, that's why — gives the result

examples.en: His father is strict and authoritarian.
He is a very respected doctor.

related.en: authoritarian — gives orders and imposes his will
authoritative, respected — trusted for knowledge and standing

note: Авторита́рный is strict and asks nobody, often negative. Авторите́тный is someone trusted for knowledge and reputation, positive.

examples.en: He has an unrequited love.
That is an irresponsible act.

related.en: unanswered, unrequited — nobody answers: безотве́тная любо́вь
irresponsible, with no sense of responsibility

note: «Irresponsible» is безотве́тственный, not безотве́тный. Безотве́тный is said of a love or a plea that gets no answer.

examples.ru: В [бу́дние] дни я встаю в семь.
examples.en: On weekdays I get up at seven.
That is ordinary everyday life.

related.en: working, of a weekday — бу́дний день, по бу́дням
everyday, ordinary, sometimes dull

note: Only бу́дний means «weekday» in the calendar. Бу́дничный describes what is everyday and routine, with no link to the calendar.

examples.en: This is my ex-husband.
He is a seasoned man, you won't fool him.
We were remembering the past.

related.en: former, ex- — бы́вший муж, бы́вшая жена́
experienced, seasoned — a man who has seen a lot
bygone, of the past — было́е вре́мя (literary)

note: Бы́вший is «former» and stands before the noun: бы́вший президе́нт. Быва́лый is said of experience, было́й of the distant past.

examples.en: I like to lie in a hot bath.
The towel is in the bathroom.

related.en: bathtub — what you bathe in
bathroom — the room

note: Ва́нная is the room (ва́нная ко́мната), ва́нна is the tub itself. In Russian flats the ва́нная and the туале́т are often two separate rooms.

examples.en: Take a deep breath in.
A heavy sigh was heard.

related.en: inhalation — the air you breathe in
sigh — of sadness, tiredness or relief

note: The verbs go the same way: вдохну́ть is «to breathe in», вздохну́ть is «to sigh».

examples.en: Please fill out the form.
She filled the glass with water.
I want to top up my account.
He added to my answer.

related.en: to fill in an empty space or a form — запо́лнить анке́ту
to fill a container — напо́лнить стака́н
to replenish what has been used up — попо́лнить счёт
to add what is missing, to supplement — допо́лнить отве́т

note: Запо́лнить is for forms and empty spaces, напо́лнить for containers. Попо́лнить is to replenish what was used up: попо́лнить запа́сы.

examples.en: He had a hostile look.
The plane was shot down by an enemy missile.

related.en: hostile, unfriendly in attitude — вражде́бный взгляд
enemy, belonging to the enemy — вра́жеская а́рмия

note: Вражде́бный describes an attitude and feelings (a look, a tone), вра́жеский what belongs to the enemy in a war.

examples.en: I spent a long time choosing a gift.
Citizens elect the president.

related.en: to choose, to pick from what is offered — pf. вы́брать
to elect by vote to an office — pf. избра́ть

note: For a personal choice (a gift, clothes, a route) say выбира́ть. Избира́ть is voting: вы́боры are «elections».

examples.en: I paid for lunch.
You can pay the bill by card.
I paid the fine at the bank.
The company paid the salary on time.

related.en: to pay for something you received — заплати́ть за обе́д
to pay a bill or a service — оплати́ть счёт
to pay in to an account, at a bank or cashier — уплати́ть штраф
to pay out a salary, pension or debt — вы́платить зарпла́ту

note: When you pay: заплати́ть, оплати́ть, уплати́ть. When a company or the state pays out: вы́платить - вы́платить пе́нсию.

examples.en: They raised three children.
He decided to grow a beard.
The athlete wants to build up muscle.

related.en: to raise a child, to grow a plant — вы́растить ребёнка
to let hair or a beard grow — отрасти́ть бо́роду
to build up, to increase — нарасти́ть мы́шцы

note: With no object, when something just grows, use вы́расти: он вы́рос - he grew up.

examples.en: The company submitted its annual report.
He signed up for a one-year course.
We have a one-year-old son.

related.en: annual, for the whole year — годово́й отчёт
lasting a year — годи́чный курс
one year old — годова́лый ребёнок

note: Annual leave is ежего́дный о́тпуск, not годово́й о́тпуск.

examples.en: This is an effective medicine.
Do you have a valid ticket?
The law in force prohibits this.

related.en: effective, efficient — де́йственное сре́дство
valid; real, actual — действи́тельный биле́т
operating, working, in force — де́йствующий зако́н

note: The verb is де́йствовать: лека́рство де́йствует - the medicine works. The adverb действи́тельно means «really, indeed».

examples.en: I have a business meeting today.
You gave sound advice.

related.en: business, work-related — делова́я встре́ча, делово́й костю́м
sensible, useful, smart — де́льный сове́т

note: Both come from де́ло but are not mixed up: делово́й is about business, де́льный about something being sensible and useful.

examples.en: There is a long corridor here.
A long flight awaits us.

related.en: long in space — дли́нный коридо́р
lasting, prolonged, rather formal — дли́тельный перелёт

note: «Long» is дли́нный for space and дли́тельный for lasting time. In speech до́лгий is more common for time: до́лгий разгово́р.

examples.en: We had a frank, confidential talk.
Children are very trusting.

related.en: confidential, frank — довери́тельный разгово́р
trusting, gullible — дове́рчивый ребёнок

note: Дове́рчивый is a trait of a person who believes easily and so is easy to deceive. Довери́тельный describes a relationship or tone in which people trust each other.

examples.en: The autumn was rainy this year.
We collected rainwater.

related.en: rain-, coming from rain — дождева́я вода́
rainy, with a lot of rain — дождли́вый день

note: Only дождли́вый means «full of rain»: дождли́вое ле́то. Дождево́й is the adjective of дождь: дождево́й червь - earthworm.

examples.en: That was friendly advice.
Russia and Serbia are friendly countries.
We have a close-knit family.

related.en: friendly, between people — дру́жеский сове́т
friendly, between states — дру́жественная страна́
close-knit, united, harmonious — дру́жная семья́

note: Дру́жный is not «friendly» but «united, harmonious»: a дру́жная кома́нда works together without quarrels.

examples.en: He is our only son.

examples.ru: В Москве есть [еди́ный] билет на метро и автобус.
examples.en: In Moscow there is a single ticket for the metro and the bus.
The prisoner is in a solitary cell.

related.en: only, sole — еди́нственный сын
single, unified as a whole — еди́ный биле́т
single, individual, solitary — одино́чная ка́мера

note: Еди́нственный means «the only one», not «unique» in the sense of exceptional: that is уника́льный.

examples.en: You are our welcome guest.
Today it is advisable to wear a warm jacket.

related.en: desired, dear, welcome — жела́нный гость
desirable, advisable — жела́тельно прийти́ зара́нее

note: Жела́тельно is often used as an impersonal word: жела́тельно прийти́ - it is advisable to come.

examples.en: He is a cruel man.
The mattress is too hard.

related.en: cruel, ruthless — жесто́кий челове́к
hard, stiff; strict, harsh — жёсткая крова́ть

note: Жёсткий is hard (жёсткое мя́со - tough meat) and strict (жёсткие усло́вия - harsh terms), жесто́кий is cruel.

examples.en: He is a skilled cook.
These are artificial flowers.

related.en: skillful, masterly — иску́сный ма́стер
artificial, man-made — иску́сственные цветы́

note: Both come from иску́сство («art, skill»): иску́сный is skillful, иску́сственный is man-made.

examples.en: What a boor! He didn't even say hello.
He is a complete ignoramus in music.

related.en: boor, rude person, lacking manners
ignoramus, uneducated person

note: A memory aid: неве́жа lacks politeness (ве́жливый), неве́жда lacks knowledge (ве́дать).

examples.en: The toothache became unbearable.
He is very impatient.

examples.ru: У него [нетерпи́мое] отношение к чужому мнению.
examples.en: He is intolerant of other people's opinions.

related.en: unbearable — нестерпи́мая боль
impatient — can't wait
intolerant of others; unacceptable

note: A memory aid: нетерпели́вый can't wait, нестерпи́мый hurts, нетерпи́мый does not accept.

examples.en: Today is a very successful day.
He is a very lucky person.

related.en: successful, well chosen — уда́чный день, уда́чная шу́тка
lucky, always succeeding — уда́чливый челове́к

note: «Happy» in the sense of joyful is счастли́вый, not уда́чный; уда́ча is «luck».

examples.en: We discussed the plan for tomorrow.
The court sentenced him to two years.

related.en: to discuss, to talk over — обсуди́ть пла́ны
to condemn, to sentence — осуди́ть на два го́да

note: Do not mix them up: обсуди́ть is to discuss, осуди́ть is to sentence or to blame. Likewise обсужде́ние - discussion, осужде́ние - condemnation.

examples.en: He can't tell truth from lies.
It is hard to tell colors apart in the dark.

related.en: to distinguish one thing from another — отлича́ть оригина́л от ко́пии
to make out, to see the difference — различа́ть цвета́

note: «To differ from» is отлича́ться от + gen.: она́ отлича́ется от сестры́. Различа́ть is «to make out, tell apart», as in различа́ть цвета́.

examples.en: The explanation was very clear.
He is a quick student.

related.en: understandable, clear — поня́тное объясне́ние
quick, bright, grasps things fast — поня́тливый учени́к

note: Поня́тно! in conversation means «I see, got it».

examples.en: That was a brave act.
He was fired for such a misdemeanor.

related.en: act, deed — смелый посту́пок
misdemeanor, minor offense — дисциплина́рный просту́пок

note: A court case is not посту́пок but проце́сс. Посту́пок is a person's act, просту́пок is a minor offense of theirs.

examples.en: He lived to a venerable age.
He answered in a respectful tone.
He was the guest of honor at the celebration.

related.en: venerable, esteemed — почте́нный во́зраст
respectful, showing respect — почти́тельный тон
honorary, of honor — почётный гость

note: Почётный is «honorary»: почётный гражданин. Почти́тельный shows respect, while почте́нный is someone who deserves it.

examples.en: There were salads on the festive table.
Don't ask idle questions.

related.en: festive, holiday — пра́здничный сто́л
idle, pointless — пра́здный вопро́с

note: Пра́здный means «idle, pointless», not «festive»; «holiday» is пра́здник.

examples.en: We have a practical class today.
The bag is very practical.

related.en: relating to practice, as opposed to theory — практи́ческая рабо́та
useful and easy to use — практи́чная вещь

note: English «practical» covers both: практи́ческий is «from practice», практи́чный is «easy to use».

examples.en: The company provided me with an apartment.
Allow me to introduce my friend to you.

related.en: to provide, to make available — предоста́вить кварти́ру
to introduce someone; to imagine — предста́вить дру́га

note: Предста́вить also means «to imagine»: предста́вь себе́ - imagine. Предоста́вить is «to provide» a right, lodging or time.

examples.en: This is a very hearty lunch.
I'm already full.

related.en: hearty, filling — сы́тный обе́д
full, having eaten enough — я сыт

note: A dish or meal is сы́тный; a person who has eaten enough is сыт.

examples.en: He is a very humane boss.
That is a human error.

related.en: humane, kind to people — челове́чное отноше́ние
human, relating to people — челове́ческая жизнь

note: Челове́чный is someone who behaves kindly and warmly, челове́ческий is everything that belongs to a human being: челове́ческая приро́да.

examples.en: He studies economics.
This will save time.

related.en: economy; the science of economics — росси́йская эконо́мика
saving, economy of resources — эконо́мия вре́мени

note: «A saving» is эконо́мия, and «to save» is эконо́мить: эконо́мить де́ньги.

examples.en: An economic crisis began in the country.
We have an economical car.
My mom is very thrifty.

related.en: economic — экономи́ческий кри́зис
economical, cheap to run — экономи́чная маши́на
thrifty, frugal (of a person) — эконо́мный челове́к

note: The adjective of эконо́мика is only экономи́ческий. Экономи́чный and эконо́мный come from эконо́мия.

examples.en: This is an effective way.
She is wearing a striking dress.

related.en: effective, gets results — эффекти́вный ме́тод
striking, makes a strong impression by its looks — эффе́ктная вне́шность

note: Эффекти́вный is judged by results, эффе́ктный by looks.

examples.en: We moved to a neighboring town.
The neighbor's dog had puppies.

related.en: neighboring, next-door — сосе́дний го́род
the neighbor's, belonging to a neighbor — сосе́дская соба́ка

note: Сосе́дний is what lies next to you (сосе́дняя ко́мната), сосе́дский what belongs to the су́сед.

examples.en: The match was played at an ice arena.
An icy wind is blowing outside.

related.en: ice-, of ice, in names and sports — ледо́вая аре́на
icy, ice-cold — ледяна́я вода́

note: Ледяно́й is said of what is as cold as ice or made of ice, also ледяно́й взгляд. Ледо́вый is for names: ледо́вый дворе́ц.

examples.ru: Он мой лучший [друг], мы вместе с детства.
examples.en: He is my best friend, we have been together since childhood.

examples.ru: Это не друг, а просто [прия́тель] с работы.
examples.en: He's not a real friend, just a buddy from work.

related.en: close friend — someone you can count on
buddy, pal — someone you get on with, but not necessarily close

note: Друг is a stronger word than «friend»: you call someone друг only if he is really close. A casual friend is прия́тель.

examples.en: What is your surname? - Petrova.
There are four people in our family.

related.en: surname, family name
family, household

note: A trap: фами́лия is only a surname, never «family». Relatives, the extended family, are родня́.

skip: false-friend article for Serbian speakers; the two words are not confusable for English speakers
pure Serbian-Russian false friend (Serbian бука = noise)
pure Serbian-Russian false friend (Serbian порез = tax)

examples.ru: Девочка заплела [косу́] и пошла в школу.
examples.en: The girl braided her hair and went to school.
She has long dark hair.

related.en: braid; also a scythe
hair on the head — used only in the plural

note: A single hair is «во́лос». The saying «нашла́ коса́ на ка́мень» (literally "the scythe hit a stone") means that two stubborn sides have met their match.
